ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Spanish Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation sanctions list, and Banco de España warnings; enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons under Ley 10/2010 Article 14, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and PEPs in international organizations; screening must be performed at onboarding, before incorporation, and on a continuous risk-based basis; source of funds and source of wealth verification via notarized declarations and bank references is mandatory for all UBOs owning 25% or more; report of suspicious operations (ROS) must be filed through SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) before any corporate registry filing if red flags exist.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (https://www.rmc.es/) and the electronic platform for name reservation via Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed exclusively in Spanish or any official language of the autonomous communities for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, but the statutory suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' is mandatory; acronyms and latinized transliteration of foreign names are permitted if the name is capable of clear pronunciation in Spanish; names must not contain expressions contrary to law, offensive terms, or misleading references to public bodies; transliteration into Latin script is required for names originating in non-Latin scripts; the exclusive use of English-language tokens is restricted unless the name is a valid international brand name and is presented with a Spanish descriptor of the corporate purpose.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España (when used as a public authority reference only)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Central Mercantile Registry issues a negative certification or rejects a name, the applicant may file a written appeal before the Director of the Registro Mercantil Central within 15 business days of the rejection notice, invoking the right to a new name; for disputed names, the applicant may also file an administrative claim before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice; if the rejection is based on similarity with a prior registered name, the applicant may request a formal report from the Registro Mercantil Central and propose a distinctive variant; the reservation may be renewed for an additional 30 days upon payment of the corresponding tariff, but a renewal requires a new application and is subject to the registry's existing prior-rights database; after final administrative exhaustion, judicial review is available under the Ley 29/2015, de 30 de julio, de Jurisdicción Voluntaria and the Ley 39/2015 on common administrative procedure, subject to 2-month filing deadline in the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used for initial registration only if the address corresponds to the registered office that appears in the public registry and is a physical Spanish address where the company's legal representative can receive official notifications; for a B2B virtual card issuer regulated by Banco de España, a fully virtual office is impermissible because the requirements under Article 14 of Ley 10/2010 and Article 3 of Royal Decree 778/2023 demand a permanent physical establishment, compliance staff, and risk-management presence in Spain; use of a co-working or serviced office is permissible only when it includes a dedicated physical administrative contact, premises access for regulators, and a genuine management site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – Unannounced physical on-site inspections by Banco de España and SEPBLAC are performed as part of Pillar 1 AML supervision; for high-risk e-money and payment institutions, the probability of an inspection within 12 months of licensing exceeds 60% if the entity holds an electronic money license under Law 21/2011; during pre-incorporation due diligence and license application, local visits by the National Securities Market Commission or Banco de España inspectors are likely unless the registered office passes a documented remote-inspection protocol.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (Articles 1-5 on incorporation, minimum capital, and governance)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de la Sociedad
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €3,000 fully paid-up upon incorporation and deposited in a Spanish bank account; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada resolves unanimously as follows: (1) The entire share capital of three thousand euros (€3,000) is subscribed by the shareholders in accordance with their shareholding agreements, with contributions paid in cash and deposited in a Spanish bank account. (2) The registered office is adopted at [full registered address], to serve as the principal place of business for virtual card issuing and spend management operations. (3) [Name] is appointed as Managing Director and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, with full powers to represent the Company and file all incorporation and licensing documents. (4) All resolutions are adopted in compliance with the Articles of Association and applicable Spanish law. This resolution shall remain valid until revoked by a subsequent Board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public followed by electronic submission to Registro Mercantil Central
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in Spanish language detailing share capital, object of the company as virtual card issuer, and governance. Execute before a Spanish notary public, pay notary fees, obtain the public deed. Then, submit electronically via the Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central portal, including the deed, proof of capital deposit, shareholder IDs, and payment of filing fees.
required_dossiers: Public Deed of Constitution (Escritura de Constitución)
Proof of payment of minimum capital (€3,000)
Shareholder identification and tax ID documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the applicant may submit additional documentation or request rectification within 10 business days through the electronic portal or administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización como Prestador de Servicios de Emisión de Medios de Pago

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agencia Española de Protección del Medio Ambiente y la Calidad del Mar (Spanish Environment Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No physical operations or emissions; virtual card issuance involves no wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling. Compliance limited to general office environmental regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections for the registered office premises; workplace safety clearance for administrative operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official electronic portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es, including the Customs and Special Taxes Department for export declarations and the Central VAT Management Office for VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (ES_SL): the foreign beneficial owner obtains a Spanish NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero); the company is incorporated by public deed before a notary and inscribed in the Mercantile Registry; within one month of registration, the company must submit Form 036 (Declaración censal / Solicitud de NIF) to AEAT, signed by a legal representative with a valid power of attorney; AEAT then issues the definitive corporate NIF in CIF format (letter plus eight digits). If the entity must transact before the definitive NIF is issued, a provisional NIF is used. A non-resident foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment may alternatively apply for a non-resident NIF (NIF-N) through Form 036/030, accompanied by the NIE of its representative, constitutional documents, and a foreign tax residence certificate; a tax representative is mandatory where the non-resident is required to file VAT or income tax and has no permanent establishment in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a resident S.L. is taxed as a separate juridical person under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) on worldwide income at a general 25% rate (15% for qualifying newly created companies for the first two years on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable income). No pass-through treatment is available; the S.L. is not a Tax Exempt Zone entity absent a specific Canary Islands ZEC incentive.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or transparent election is available for a Spanish S.L. Hybrid mismatch rules are codified in Law 27/2014 (Corporate Income Tax Law), Article 15 septies, and disallow deductions in cases involving deduction/no-inclusion or hybrid transfer outcomes between Spain and other EU/EEA jurisdictions. Fiscal transparency elections are limited to certain economic interest groupings (EIGE/EEIG) and cannot be used by the S.L. The entity may choose between standalone taxation and the Spanish tax consolidation regime only if it directly or indirectly controls one or more resident entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (VAT / Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold in local currency EUR; every taxable person carrying out a taxable activity in Spain must register from the first taxable transaction. For an EU-established business selling distance goods or B2C electronic services into Spain, an EU-wide OSS threshold of EUR 10,000 applies; once exceeded, VAT accounting and registration are required under the Spanish/OSS regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates VERI*FACTU-compliant certified billing software (Royal Decree 1007/2023) capable of generating an invariant hash and allowing near-real-time access or transmission of invoice records to AEAT. The Immediate Information Supply (SII) requires large enterprises with turnover above EUR 6,000,000 and VAT Groups to transmit VAT book records electronically within four days for simplified invoices and eight days for complete invoices, depending on the record type. B2B e-invoicing in a structured FacturaE XML format under the Ley Crea y Crece is phased in from 2025/2026 based on annual turnover. Failure to comply with these electronic record requirements may affect input VAT deduction rights and trigger administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for the 0% export VAT rate under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law where: (i) goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting for their account; (ii) departure occurs within three months from the date of the supply, or within an administratively extended period; (iii) a completed Single Administrative Document (DUA/SAD) is accepted by customs; and (iv) the exporter retains transport documents such as a bill of lading, air waybill, or CMR proving physical exit. Related international services (transport, loading, handling, insurance) may also be zero-rated. For a virtual card issuer, core card issuing and payment processing services are VAT-exempt financial services rather than zero-rated supplies; cross-border B2B services to non-EU customers generally fall outside the scope of Spanish VAT under place-of-supply rules, and input VAT recovery is limited by the financial sector pro-rata rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) accepted by Agencia Tributaria - Customs and Special Taxes Department
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note proving physical exit from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/SWIFT MT103 payment evidence
Commercial invoice and packing list expressly referring to the export transaction
Export broker authorization and customs warehouse/entry records if goods were stored prior to export
Certificate of Exit, movement certificate, or Intrastat/EDIFACT export control records where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may audit export zero-rating for up to four years under the statutory limitation period. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical exit, the VAT is retrospectively assessed at 21% with late-payment interest from the original due date. A tax omission caused by negligence triggers a proportional penalty of 50% of the underdeclared VAT, reducible to 25% upon timely conformity; use of false documents or fraudulent export evidence upgrades the infringement to a serious/fraudulent procedure with a 75% penalty. Deliberate fraudulent export zero-rating may constitute an offence against the Public Treasury where the annual defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, leading to fines of up to six times the defrauded amount and imprisonment, together with reversal of any refunds, denial of monthly refund privileges, and secondary liability of administrators and customs agents under the Spanish General Tax Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem and European System of Central Banks; foreign exchange supervisory competence shared with the Spanish Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, specifically the General Directorate for International Trade and Investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Spanish Law 19/2003. No prior exchange control authorization is required for profit repatriation, dividend remittance, or liquidation proceeds. Non-resident owners may freely transfer capital; only statistical declarations to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments register are mandatory for direct investments exceeding EUR 250,000 and for any investment into Spanish entities from non-EU countries, with a one-month post-operation filing window.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds exists in Spain or the Eurozone. Spanish resident exporters may maintain foreign currency accounts both domestically and abroad; however, all cross-border transactions are subject to documentation requirements under EU Regulation 2021/1230 and Spanish CTE (Código de Tránsito Exterior) for customs/banking evidence. Payments received in foreign currency must be recorded in the beneficiary's FX account and may be settled freely to EUR or retained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR) for card scheme settlement and treasury liquidity
Sponsor Settlement Account for Mastercard/Visa direct connectivity
Capital Escrow Account for cardholder funds segregation
Operational Account (EUR) for FX hedging collateral

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High only if the external EMI is a licensed, passportable EU e-money institution or payment institution under PSD2. A Spanish SL virtual card issuer cannot rely on a non-EU offshore digital EMI for direct scheme membership or Spanish bank clearing. Such an EMI can participate only via a regulated Spanish partner bank, and the card issuer itself must hold a corresponding license (EMI or PI) from the Bank of Spain unless it uses a licensed sponsor bank. BaaS providers such as Solaris or ClearBank (EU-regulated) are viable as sponsor rails, but the issuer's AML compliance and sub-licensing arrangements must be pre-approved by the network and sponsor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a High_Risk_Special_License corporate client, physical presence of directors/signatories is effectively mandatory for account opening at Any Spanish Tier 1 bank. Remote onboarding is not available for this business scope; at least one of the following must occur: (i) in-person interview at the bank's compliance office, (ii) appearance before a Spanish notary for signature legalization, or (iii) a videographic notarial audit with apostille certification for foreign shareholders. Foreign corporate documents need legalization by the relevant consulate or apostille under the Hague Convention, and the ultimate beneficial owner identity must be disclosed to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) involves non-EU residents with layered corporate structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, full shareholder register with passport copies, group structure chart, board resolution appointing local compliance officer, audited financial statements of beneficial owners, and Spanish tax registration certificate (Modelo 036).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-currency card loads from heterogeneous sources without transparency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT program aligned with Law 10/2010, transaction monitoring engine with threshold flagging (e.g., > EUR 10,000 daily per card), source of funds proof for corporate cardholders, KYC documentation for all clients, and written procedures for provisional load limits based on business profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Departmental review of virtualization / fintech outsourcing to third-party processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service provider due diligence file, data processing agreement compliant with GDPR, segregation of client funds in an escrow account, contractual audit rights, and network compliance certificates from Mastercard/Visa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure through cross-border card acceptance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening against EU consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and UNSC lists; geoblocking rules for sanctioned territories; transaction blocking procedures with audit logs; periodic independent compliance review by an external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 'CAPITAL/DEQUIP' and must be accompanied by a Bank of Spain direct investment declaration if the amount exceeds EUR 250,000 or the investor is non-EU. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments ≤ EUR 500,000. The SL's bank account must be identified with the NIF/CIF and CNAE activity code, and the receiving bank may request a notarized board resolution and investment registration certificate within one month to evidence the nature of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For card scheme settlement, daily payouts to Mastercard/Visa are executed via the scheme's settlement bank (e.g., GIRO) using MT103 or MT202 when paired with treasury instruction codes. For merchant disbursements, SEPA Instant Credit is preferred within the Eurozone; for cross-border beneficiaries outside EUR, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'PI-1012' (card services). High-value partner B2B purchases of card inventory or sponsorship fees may be settled through commercial LC (MT700) with a bank guarantee, though this is only recommended for non-standard large contracts. All outbound payments must satisfy the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation 1493/2019 traceability requirements and Spanish Business Transaction Law 5/2013 (cash movement limit EUR 1,000).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX Forwards under ISDA/EMIR with Spanish credit institutions or branches (EUR/USD, EUR/RUB, EUR/LATAM currencies)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible currencies (BRL, ARS, TRY) with EU-regulated counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for short-term liquidity repositioning between card scheme settlement accounts
European-style European FX Options (EUR put / USD call) for risk premium management without speculative intent
Tom/Next FX swaps and forward rollovers permitted under Banco de España Circular 3/2014 for treasury cash management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and deposited within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end, generally by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure after one year of non-filing, except statutory exemptions; administrative fine generally EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, potentially up to EUR 300,000 for companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry through the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts; beneficial ownership changes must also be updated without undue delay and reflected in the applicable registry filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or missing beneficial ownership information may prevent completion of the accounts filing and may trigger registry closure, administrative liability, and anti-money-laundering enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge is generally 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, capped at 12 months; after 12 months, a 15% surcharge plus applicable interest may apply. Late filing without tax due may incur a fixed penalty, generally EUR 200, subject to statutory reductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate governance and statutory register review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; relevant Mercantile Registry for filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Conduct at least annually and before approval of the annual accounts; update registers promptly after any corporate event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete registers may impair shareholder, director, beneficial ownership, and corporate authority evidence and may result in civil, administrative, tax, or anti-money-laundering exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regulated payment or electronic-money institution annual regulatory reporting, if licensed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bank of Spain and other competent financial authorities, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic and annual deadlines prescribed by the applicable payment-services, electronic-money, prudential, safeguarding, conduct, and anti-money-laundering rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory remediation, reporting deficiencies, monetary sanctions, restrictions on activities, management measures, and potential suspension or withdrawal of the authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is generally mandatory where, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of: EUR 2.85 million total assets, EUR 5.7 million net annual turnover, or 50 average employees. Audit is also mandatory for certain regulated entities, including payment or electronic-money institutions where sector-specific rules apply, and for other statutory cases such as securities-market entities or qualifying groups.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan and applicable sector-specific Bank of Spain accounting rules. IFRS is required or permitted principally for qualifying consolidated groups and entities subject to applicable securities-market rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify, verify, document, and keep current its ultimate beneficial owners. The beneficial ownership declaration is generally submitted with the annual accounts and must be updated when ownership, control, or identifying information changes. Share transfers require corresponding updates to the Register of Members and beneficial ownership records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and persons holding powers of representation
Register of contracts between the sole shareholder and the company, if applicable
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 600-2,000 per year, approximately USD 650-2,200, depending on address, mail handling, corporate secretarial services, and regulated-business requirements.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,500-12,000 per year, approximately USD 2,700-13,000, for a standard Spanish SL; regulated payment or electronic-money businesses may require EUR 10,000-40,000 or more, approximately USD 11,000-44,000, depending on complexity and reporting scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general rate for Sociedades under Art. 29.1 LIS); 15% reduced startup rate for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base, subject to the EUR 1,000,000 annual net-turnover cap; 20% reduced rate applies to micro-entities with net turnover not exceeding EUR 1,000,000 for tax periods commencing on or after 1 January 2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime (Art. 23 LIS): 60% exemption on qualifying IP-related net income; R&D&I tax credits (Art. 35 LIS) of 25% on R&D base and up to 42% combined for technology investments; newly created SLs benefit from the 15% reduced rate; territorial bonuses for Ceuta and Melilla; participation-exemption relief for qualifying intra-group dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS); no wealth tax or net-worth tax at entity level for SLs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry under Art. 26 LIS; annual offset of tax losses is subject to cap of 50% for taxpayers with net turnover above EUR 60,000,000 and 25% for net turnover between EUR 20,000,000 and EUR 60,000,000; below EUR 20,000,000 full offset applies).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades; mandatory electronic filing via AEAT Sede Electrónica (www.agenciatributaria.gob.es), submitted through the pre-validated Form 200 XML package or online Web entry; non-resident permanent establishments use the same Form 200 with restricted boxes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax period; for a calendar-year SL, the return must be filed by 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number of the Spanish entity or permanent establishment (PE).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SL without a Spanish PE must not file Modelo 200; it files Modelo 210 for Spanish-source income. A non-resident SL with a registered PE files Form 200 using its Spanish PE NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature of the return: 1 for regular return (ingreso/devolución), 2 for refund after an unfavourable resolution, 3 for rectification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Choose 1 for the ordinary annual return of the Spanish PE; remittance of profits to the foreign head office is declared separately on Form 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before compensation of prior-year negative tax bases, computed on an accrual basis in accordance with LIS rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Spanish PE's allocable income; foreign-source income attributable to the head office is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 101 – Compensación de bases imponibles negativas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior periods offset against the current taxable base, subject to Art. 26 LIS quantitative caps.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE may offset losses generated by the PE itself in prior Spanish tax periods; losses of the foreign head office are not eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability resulting from applying the statutory rate (25%) to the taxable base, before deductions and double-taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate to PE taxable income; treaty provisions do not reduce the corporate rate but may affect profit attribution and remittance withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for international double taxation, R&D&I credits and patent-box relief, resulting in the net tax liability (cuota líquida).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require certification of the underlying foreign tax; substantiation documentation must be retained for AEAT audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 215/216 – Pagos fraccionados y cuota resultante
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (Modelo 202) made during the tax period; final balance due (a ingresar) or refundable (a devolver).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must also file quarterly Modelo 202 advance payments computed on the prior-year Form 200 liability or on accounting results.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months and 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest (3.75% in 2025); failure to file entirely is a tax infringement under Art. 198 LGT with penalties from EUR 200 to EUR 1,500; under-declaration attracts a penalty under Art. 191 LGT of 50% (leve), 100% (grave) or 150% (muy grave) of the resulting assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 – Pago fraccionado del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; electronic filing via AEAT Sede Electrónica; payment settlement can be deferred or split through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (three advance instalments for a calendar-year taxpayer)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment within the first 20 calendar days of April (first instalment), October (second instalment) and December (third instalment); all taxpayers are obliged to file even where the payment result is nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number of the SL or PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE uses the Spanish PE NIF; no quarterly filing is required for non-resident entities without a Spanish PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Method of computation: 1 if the instalment is based on the tax liability of the prior year (Art. 40.2 LIS); 2 if based on accounting profit (Art. 40.3 LIS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE generally uses method 1 in the same manner as resident SLs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate and gross instalment amount; certain entities apply special rates (15% startup, 20% micro-entity, 30% credit institutions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE of an EU parent applying the 15% startup regime may use the reduced rate only if the PE constitutes a newly created activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount payable after applying the year-to-date installments already filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts due are payable through the AEAT bank account; foreign entities must hold a Spanish bank account or use the AEAT NRC payment system.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or underpayment of a Model 202 instalment: late-filing surcharge under Art. 27 LGT (5% to 20% escalating) plus late-payment interest at 3.75%; under-declaration in a quarterly payment is sanctioned under Art. 191 LGT with a penalty of 50% to 150% of the shortfall and interest accruing from the instalment due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% statutory withholding under Art. 21 TRLIRNR on dividends and profit distributions paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident corporate shareholder; the rate is reduced to 0% for EU/EEA corporate shareholders holding at least 5% of share capital for one year under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Art. 21 TRLIRNR; domestic participation-exemption rules (Art. 21 LIS) also apply to the recipient only if the same qualifying conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief protocol: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) for the applicable fiscal year from the shareholder's resident tax authority; (ii) where the Spanish payer applied the statutory 19% at source, file AEAT Form 210 (IRNR without permanent establishment) requesting refund of excess withholding, attaching the TRC, power of attorney, payment certificates and bank confirmation; (iii) claims must be filed within the four-year statutory limitation period of Art. 66 LGT; (iv) for EU resident parents, the 0% rate can be applied at source by submitting a prior declaration of qualifying shareholding and the foreign tax residence certificate to the Spanish paying entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 19% on outbound interest and IP royalties paid by a Spanish entity to non-residents (Art. 24 TRLIRNR); 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated companies (25% minimum shareholding or voting rights held for at least one year where the recipient is an EU/EEA company); most Spanish double taxation treaties reduce royalty and interest withholding to 0%–10% (common treaty rates: interest 0%–10%, royalties 5%–10%); licenses for payment-system software embedded in virtual card programmes are routinely recharacterized as royalties if the fintech grants exploitation of pre-existing IP.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover of the Spanish taxpayer in the preceding tax period triggers mandatory Local File (Art. 13.2 LIS, RD 634/2015); Master File applies where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 45,000,000; an additional informative declaration (Modelo 232) is mandatory by 30 November following the tax period for any related-party transaction exceeding EUR 250,000 or where the aggregate of related-party operations requires filing per AEAT instructions; documentation must be kept in Spanish or English.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP – Comparable Uncontrolled Price (método del precio libre comparable)
Resale Price Method – Precio de reventa
TNMM – Transactional Net Margin Method (margen neto transaccional)
Profit Split Method – Reparto del resultado
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as in UAE; however, real economic substance is enforced through domestic GAAR (Art. 15 LGT), CFC rules (Art. 100 LIS), residency and management-and-control tests (Art. 8 LIS), and treaty anti-abuse/LOB clauses. Fintech issuers of virtual cards must demonstrate genuine commercial activity to the Bank of Spain and AEAT, including local premises, full-time qualified staff, actual treasury and risk functions, and board decision-making in Spain; a purely 'letterbox' structure will be recharacterized, its Costa Rican or LATAM counterpart disregarded, and its turnover re-attributed to the Spanish SL.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Criminal Tax Fraud (delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing interchange fee income from corporate virtual-card transactions, issuing false cost invoices from related 'technology providers', or presenting materially false expense entries causing the Spanish SL to understate taxable income by more than EUR 120,000 in a single tax period (Art. 305 Código Penal).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, fine from the amount defrauded up to six times that sum, loss of tax benefits, subsidies and public contracts for up to 4 years, publication of the conviction; where false invoices or opacity mechanisms are used, the offence is aggravated with prison of 4 to 6 years and fine of double to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability toward the Tax Administration under Art. 43.1.g LGT for corporate taxes not paid in compliance; civil action for restitution; personal embargo of assets; travel bans and surrender of passport ordered by the criminal court; disqualification from managing assets and from public office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / GAAR Abuse (sociedad pantalla; fraude de ley tributaria)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Constituting the Spanish SL purely as a conduit so that card issuing services, merchant contracts, treasury functions and executive decisions are executed in a zero-tax jurisdiction, while the SL retains only nominal private office space and a mailbox, in order to shift Spanish-source corporate income outside Spain's taxing jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the GAAR (Art. 15 LGT) to disregard the arrangement and reattribute income to Spain; recharacterization of entities, 50%–150% penalty on the resulting assessment under Art. 191 LGT plus late-payment interest; DTA relief denied under limitation-of-benefits and principal-purpose tests; referral to the CbC/Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive exchange channels for cross-border mismatch reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who established or maintained the artificial structure are personally liable under Art. 43.1.g LGT and Art. 236 LSC for the hidden tax debt; corporate veil may be pierced in the enforcement phase exposing directors' personal assets; court-imposed restrictions on leaving Spain; if the misstatement exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal responsibility under Art. 305 or Art. 306 Código Penal with prison up to 6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Payment Services and AML Non-Compliance (Banco de España enforcement)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing and acquiring virtual corporate cards, holding client funds, or executing payment transactions without the required authorisation as a payment institution or e-money institution under Law 21/2011 and Royal Decree 778/2012, combined with failure to implement AML/KYC controls for card transactions with LATAM counterparties, such as lax monitoring of sanctions-listed merchants, unaudited program managers, or anonymous cardholder structures under Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Very serious infringement under Law 21/2011: administrative fine up to EUR 5,000,000 or up to twice the profit obtained, suspension or revocation of operations, and deposit of client funds; AML infringement under Law 10/2010: fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 600,000 for serious offences, and above EUR 600,000 or up to 5% of total annual turnover for very serious offences, with requirement to correct deficiencies; repeat infringement may result in dissolution of the legal entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto managers are personally liable for AML sanctions-imposed amounts under Art. 51 Law 10/2010; the National Court (Audiencia Nacional) may order occupational disqualification, provisional detention pending charge, freezing of personal bank accounts, and prosecution for money laundering (Art. 302 Código Penal) with imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years for the actual operator.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Hidden Profit Repatriation (knowing non-arm's-length dealings)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Spanish SL excessive software royalties, management fees, or intercompany Card Network access fees from a foreign related party, or granting interest-free intercompany loans to a parent in a no-withholding jurisdiction, thereby stripping nearly all Spanish taxable profit and avoiding the EUR 250,000 Modelo 232 reporting threshold deliberately through invoice splitting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT adjustment to arm's length price under Art. 18 LIS; recharacterization of excessive payments as hidden dividends, royalties or interest subject to 19% withholding; penalty for inadequate transfer-pricing documentation under Art. 18.13 LIS of EUR 1,500 per tax period plus 50%–150% penalty on the adjustment where documentation was absent or materially false; interest accrues from the filing date; potential referral to the Economic-Crimes Prosecutor if the evasion exceeds EUR 120,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or signed the mispriced intercompany contracts face joint and several liability for the resulting corporate tax shortfall under Art. 43.1.g LGT; civil liability action by the company for breach of fiduciary duty under Art. 236 LSC; criminal exposure as accomplices or media of Art. 305 Código Penal where the intended mispricing is proven, carrying prison of 2 to 6 years and mandatory restitution of defrauded sums.
